DRY adversary FAILED the rules with this confirmed finding (verified against the code): NoCallerFilePathAnalyzer.AnalyzeAttribute (analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/NoCallerFilePathAnalyzer.cs:76-90) duplicates the ENTIRE AnalyzeAttribute method body of InteropOnlyInCrossPlatformLibrariesAnalyzer (AG0008, analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/InteropOnlyInCrossPlatformLibrariesAnalyzer.cs:69-84). The two are identical except for (a) the identity set passed to AttributeIdentity.IsAnyOf — CallerFilePathAttribute (AG0039) vs PInvoke.InteropAttributes (AG0008) — and (b) the DiagnosticDescriptor passed to Diagnostic.Create.

FIX (rails-dry-code rail 6, extract-one-owner — do exactly this, nothing more): extract the shared 'match an applied attribute by an identity set and report a descriptor' sequence — cast context.Node to AttributeSyntax, return early unless AttributeIdentity.IsAnyOf(context.SemanticModel, attribute, <identitySet>, ct) matches, else compute the qualified name via AttributeSyntaxName.FullName(AttributeSyntaxName.SimpleName(attribute.Name)) and context.ReportDiagnostic(Diagnostic.Create(<descriptor>, attribute.GetLocation(), qualifiedName)) — into ONE shared static owner (a new helper type under analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers/, e.g. an AppliedAttributeBan.Report(context, identitySet, descriptor) method, named per the repo's conventions). Route BOTH AG0008 and AG0039 through that one owner: each analyzer's registered SyntaxNodeAction becomes a thin call passing its own identity set and Rule descriptor. Leave NO copy of the sequence in either analyzer. Note AG0008 keeps its CompilationStart gate and GeneratedCodeAnalysisFlags.Analyze; only the duplicated match-then-report body moves to the shared owner. Do not change any rule's behavior, id, message, or the RED surface.

Re-prove: AG0039 still fires RED at exactly tests/AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests/Presence/Linux/PolkitPolicyIntegrityTests.cs:55 on the linux-arm64 build; the default macOS solution build stays 0/0; the AG0039 and AG0035 analyzer unit tests all pass; AG0008's existing tests still pass.
